english.title: Dishonestly cause / allow a recipient to fail to give prompt notification of a change in circumstances
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) dishonestly caused or allowed **(..SPECIFY THE RECIPIENT..) who was a person in receipt of a benefit, payment or advantage, namely **(..SPECIFY THE BENEFIT / PAYMENT / ADVANTAGE..), under **(..SPECIFY THE PROVISION OF SOCIAL SECURITY LEGISLATION..), to fail to give a prompt notification to

(A)_[the Department for Work and Pensions]_
(B)_[a local authority, namely **(.. SPECIFY THE AUTHORITY..)]_

of a change in circumstances that you knew would affect the claimant's entitlement, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PARTICULARS OF CHANGES OF CIRCUMSTANCES..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 111A(1E) and (1G)(3) of the Social Security Administration Act 1992.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Seven years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
